Status: Admitted. Effective severity follows the shared core/shell/default policy.

## What caused the finding, and why it matters

A public property on a record exposes a public `set` accessor rather than
`init`. A caller can change it after creation, so code sharing the record may
observe different values without an explicit new value or transition.

## Before

```csharp
public sealed record Expense
{
    public decimal Total { get; set; }
}
```

## After

```csharp
public sealed record Expense
{
    public decimal Total { get; init; }
}
```

## Inspection and limits

The rule inspects property/containing-type symbols, the record shape and public
setter accessibility. Ordinary mutable classes are outside this restricted rule.
`init` prevents later property assignment; it does not freeze referenced objects.
An init-only `List<string>` can still be changed through the list reference.
A record is not proof that its entire object graph is immutable. CSAI0002 checks
selected collection types separately; neither rule proves business correctness.

## Framework boundary

Keep serializer/ORM/framework mutation in an honestly declared shell when its
contract requires it, then map into the domain. Do not move expense policy into
the shell or widen scope merely to hide a finding. Declared shell findings stay
visible; a complete verifier run still checks scope and required evidence.

## Code fix and compatibility

The explicit IDE action **Use init accessor** proposes the restricted
set-to-init auto-property edit. It declines setters with bodies. Preview it:
post-construction assignments, interfaces, serializers, binding and persistence
contracts may break. It does not migrate callers or preserve behavior by proof.
Run the affected builds/tests; no unattended CLI fix is provided.

## Evidence and grants

`specimens/Native.Bad/CSAI0001/`. The guide's two examples also compile in tests.
Suppressing the diagnostic requires its exact fingerprint and an authorized

public sealed record Batch(List<string> Items);","codeSha256":"737fe1b324d9532ff4ac3b2644e8af06e204bcb39e68d14ada4923c0a8c65596","guide":"# CSAI0002 — A record exposes a mutable collection

Status: Admitted. Effective severity follows the shared core/shell/default policy.

## What caused the finding, and why it matters

A public record property exposes an array or a known mutable collection.
Changing elements through a shared collection reference can change a record's
observed contents even when its property cannot be reassigned.

## Before

```csharp
using System.Collections.Generic;
public sealed record Batch(List<string> Items);
```

## After

```csharp
using System.Collections.Immutable;
public sealed record Batch(ImmutableArray<string> Items);
```

## Inspection and limits

The rule checks public record property type metadata: arrays, ArrayList,
Hashtable, ICollection/IList/IDictionary, their generic forms, List, Dictionary,
HashSet, Collection and ObservableCollection. Custom types are not guessed to be
immutable or mutable. An immutable container can still contain mutable objects;
this is not recursive object-graph validation. Default collection values and
business invariants need their own validation/tests. An interface with fewer
mutation methods does not establish ownership of the underlying collection.

## Framework boundary

A framework collection contract may belong in a declared serializer/ORM shell.
Convert/copy deliberately when crossing into the core. Do not relocate business
rules or grant exemptions simply to pass. Shell observations remain visible.

## Code fix and compatibility

No code fix is supplied. Choose ownership, copying, allocation, ordering and
serialization semantics with the caller. The example changes the contract;
update constructors and serializers and execute the relevant tests.

Status: Admitted. Disabled nullable flow also leaves compiler evidence incomplete.

## What caused the finding, and why it matters

The compilation lacks the full nullable context, or source contains
`#nullable disable`. The compiler then cannot supply the nullable-flow evidence
required by this policy. Annotations-only and warnings-only modes are not the
full enabled context.

## Before

```csharp
#nullable disable
public static class Names
{
    public static int Length(string name) => name.Length;
}
```

## After

```csharp
#nullable enable
public static class Names
{
    public static int Length(string name) => name.Length;
}
```

## Inspection and limits

The rule reads compilation nullable options and disable directives. Enable
`<Nullable>enable</Nullable>` at project scope as well; the tiny example isolates
the directive. Fix resulting warnings by checking inputs or modeling absence.
Enabling the compiler does not prove runtime input is non-null or all paths safe.
Validate untrusted data at a real boundary; `!` erases evidence instead.

## Framework boundary

Framework nullable DTOs can stay in a declared shell and map into the core.
Keep flow analysis enabled there too: a shell or grant does not manufacture the
missing compiler evidence. Never move arbitrary domain behavior to avoid this
requirement or disable warnings to obtain green output.

## Code fix and compatibility

No automatic fix. Enabling nullable analysis can reveal existing warnings and
change annotated contracts. Review callers and framework mapping and run tests.

the compiler's responsibility; these declarations require the pinned preview SDK.

input into an explicit core outcome. Do not move business behavior into shell to
escape findings. A null check preserves evidence; `!` does not validate input.
